subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should plain `message(action="send")` prevent models from seeing poll creation fields, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: Current code intentionally accepts schema-padded poll metadata but still rejects non-empty poll content fields; changing that boundary affects shared channel delivery semantics across Feishu, Telegram, Discord, Slack, and other message-tool channels.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while keeping strict poll validation.

options.title: Strip poll params on send
options.body: Treat action="send" as authoritative and drop poll fields before delivery, improving reliability but potentially masking poll-intent mistakes.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields on send and require schema discovery or callers to avoid generating them accidentally.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while keeping strict poll validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll-guard and schema-consistency work is the strongest history signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
